DEVIATION REPORT - Cascadia/Eurocloud DTA markup (privileged; for M. Chen, due May 20, 2025). Matter no. differs: email 2025-0412, playbook LH-2025-0482 (reconcile).

BOTTOM LINE
1. Do not counter on this paper. 13 Walk Away clusters (Part 1). Playbook s2.2/6.4: no counter-proposal until you authorize; fallbacks below are for your approval only.
2. The markup is not a true redline of our April 14 draft: its baseline text and numbering differ, its "47 changes" appendix omits about 25 tracked edits, and untracked deletions exist (Part 4). Demand a machine compare against April 14 and reserve rights.
3. Together the changes defeat the April 2 TIA (CHS-TIA-2025-001 s7.2 Conditions 1-3: contractual measures preserved, SCCs unmodified, no unassessed jurisdictions). The TIA covers the U.S. only.

PART 1 - WALK AWAY (REJECT). Format: markup clause (original clause) | original | markup | playbook | risk | response.

1. Breach notice, 9.1 and 1.1 (orig 7.1). Original: 24h from "becoming aware." Markup: 72h from "confirming"; breach exists only if "confirmed following a reasonable internal investigation." Playbook 4.1: Preferred 24h; Acceptable 36h; Walk Away over 48h or any "confirming" trigger, so double violation. Risk: Art 33(2) requires notice "without undue delay after becoming aware," with no 72h allowance; Eurocloud controls the clock; Cascadia's own Art 33(1) 72h filing (Art 83(4)(a) fines) loses its buffer. Eurocloud's comment conflates Art 33(1) and 33(2). Fallback: 36h from becoming aware (including suspected breach), phased updates per orig 7.3, restore phone escalation, delete definition insert.

2. Sub-processors, 6.1-6.2, 5.1 "including its Affiliates" (orig 8, SCC cl.9). Original: specific consent, 30 days, objection binds. Markup: general authorization; 14 days' notice; 10-day objection; 5-day resolution; sole remedy termination of whole DTA on 30 days. Playbook 4.2: Walk Away under 20 days and sole-remedy termination (both hit). Risk: illusory Art 28(2) control; with 24.5 early-termination fees, objecting could cost money. Fallback (Acceptable): general authorization, 30 days with full information, objection on reasonable grounds, then no engagement or termination of affected services only, no fees; non-EEA sub-processors need consent; strike "Affiliates."

3. Localization, 6.5, 7.1, "Operational Facilities," Annex II item 6, Annex III (orig 6.1-6.3, 13.5). Original: EEA only; no remote access or mirroring outside EEA. Markup: processing at any facility, including Singapore and Sao Paulo; Annex III pre-approves Eurocloud Solutions Pte. Ltd. and Eurocloud Brasil Servicos de Tecnologia Ltda. Playbook 4.6 Walk Away (a) blanket clause, (b) non-adequate countries, (c) not in TIA. Risk: Chapter V breach (Art 44; Art 83(5)(c) up to EUR 20M/4%); no Art 45 decision for Singapore/Brazil per playbook (verify at signing; unverified). Fallback: EEA default; DR only in Art 45-adequate locations listed in annex; anything else needs prior written consent after new TIA, SCCs, supplementary measures. Specialists in Singapore/Brazil law only if Eurocloud shows genuine need.

4. Transfer mechanism and TIA, 7.2, 7.4 (orig 13.1-13.5). Markup: Eurocloud picks mechanism "in its reasonable discretion" (adequacy, SCCs, BCRs, Art 49 derogations); TIA only "where the parties mutually agree." Playbook 4.10: Preferred TIA before transfer; Acceptable within 30 days with no transfer until completed; plus 4.6(c). Risk: Art 49 derogations cannot carry systematic transfers (EDPB Guidelines 2/2018); no approved BCRs identified; Schrems II (C-311/18) and SCC cl.14 require assessment, so "only an EDPB recommendation" is wrong. Response: reinstate 13.2/13.5; SCCs remain backbone; 7.3 DPF-secondary language is acceptable as drafted.

5. Audit, 10.1-10.2 (orig 15). Original: unlimited on-site, 10 business days' notice; certifications supplementary only. Markup: annual SOC 2 (Thornbury), ISO 27001, DPO summary "satisfy in full" Art 28(3)(h); on-site clause deleted. Playbook 4.3 Walk Away: certification-only and "satisfy in full." Risk: Art 28(3)(h) says "including inspections"; Art 5(2) accountability for special category data. Fallback: one annual focused on-site audit at Cascadia's cost plus cause-based audits (breach, regulator inquiry, material sub-processor change) at Eurocloud's cost where breach-driven; certifications supplement routine review; address multi-tenant security with escorted, scoped access and third-party auditor under NDA.

6. Deletion, 13.1-13.2 (orig 16). Original: 30 days; officer certificate (dates, method, no copies). Markup: 180 days; certificate deleted; new 13.2 lets Eurocloud keep encrypted backups 30 days after "primary deletion" (up to about 210 days), no certificate. Playbook 4.4: Acceptable 60 days plus 30 backup with written confirmation; Walk Away over 90 days or no certification (both hit). Risk: Art 28(3)(g); SCC cl.8.5 itself requires certification, so the "not required by GDPR" comment is wrong. Fallback: 60 days plus up to 30 backup, officer certificate within 10 business days covering backups, NIST SP 800-88.

7. Liability, 15.3, 16.2 (orig 18.3, 17.3). Original: 2x fees (Year 1 EUR 8.4M); data protection uncapped. Markup: cap applies to everything. Playbook 4.5 Walk Away (b): data protection under general cap without enhancement. Risk: one incident exhausts EUR 8.4M of a EUR 15.6M deal against fines up to EUR 20M/4% (Art 83(5)) and Art 82 claims; cap cannot bind data subjects (Art 82(4); SCC cl.12). Eurocloud offers an "enhanced cap," so open at uncapped, then fall back to separate ring-fenced 3x annual fees (Year 1 EUR 12.6M) for data protection, breach, transfer and personal-data confidentiality claims.

8. Fine indemnity, 16.3 (orig 17.1-17.2). Original: mutual; each bears own fines. Markup: Cascadia-only indemnity for processor fines "attributable" to instructions, any controller non-compliance or any inaccurate s4 warranty; survives termination; reciprocal clause gone. Playbook 4.11 Walk Away: one-sided. Risk: Eurocloud could shift its own Art 28/32 fines. Response: delete; restore mutual fault-based indemnity "to the extent lawful" (Irish-law enforceability unresolved; consult Irish counsel); fines within 3x cap; if mutuality fails, delete fine indemnities entirely (playbook preference).

9. DPIA, 11.3 deleted (orig 11.3). Playbook 4.9 Walk Away. Risk: Art 28(3)(f), 35(3)(b) (500,000 rising to 1.8M subjects); markup 5.5 adds "commercially reasonable and technically feasible." Eurocloud's comment ignores 28(3)(f). Fallback: 15 business days, written DPO input, follow-ups within 10; DPIA must finish before August 1 go-live.

10. DPO, 12.1, recital I (orig 12). Original: direct, 5 business days, email. Markup: registered post to Harcourt Street only; 20 business days. Playbook 4.8 Walk Away (over 15 days; registered-post-only), effectively 25+. Fallback: 10 business days, email mandatory (TIA lists dpo@eurocloudsolutions.ie), post optional, 24/7 incident contact; recital I acceptable.

11. SCC integrity, Annex IV modification paragraph, 28.8 (orig 13.6-13.7). Markup: parties "may agree to modify" SCCs; conflicts resolved by "good faith" negotiation (original: SCCs prevail). Untracked: cl.9 switched from Option 1 specific to Option 2 general authorization; cl.12 "subject to Section 15"; cl.7 docking "not elected." Playbook 4.10 Walk Away (b); TIA Condition 2: modification voids Art 46(2)(c) basis. Response: delete; restore 13.7 and SCC prevailing; annex verbatim SCC text.

12. Governing law, 26.1-26.2, Annex IV cl.17-18, 14.3 (orig 26). Markup: Singapore law, SIAC, three arbitrators, Singapore seat. Playbook 4.7 Walk Away (non-EU law, non-EU arbitration). Risk: Module Two cl.17-18 require an EU Member State's law and courts (from memory; EUR-Lex fetch blocked, unverified), so this breaks the SCCs; arbitral confidentiality hinders supervisory cooperation. Eurocloud says its parent is Singapore-headquartered, yet Annex III calls the Singapore/Brazil entities its subsidiaries; request group structure. Non-starter; fallback only another EU Member State law and courts. Irish counsel to confirm.

13. Anonymization, 5.6, "Anonymized Data," 2.7 (orig 2.5 bars own-purpose use). Markup: Eurocloud may anonymize and use data for product development, benchmarking, marketing; outside GDPR. Playbook 4.12 Walk Away (marketing; no standard, verification, oversight). Risk: anonymizing is processing needing instructions; Eurocloud becomes controller (Art 28(10)); definition ("without additional information") describes pseudonymization (Art 4(5)), not Recital 26; biometric/mental-health data resist anonymization; HIPAA 45 CFR 164.514 stricter. Delete. Only with partner approval: Cascadia-approved methodology, dual Recital 26 plus 164.514 standard, independent verification, no marketing, audit coverage.

PART 2 - OUTSIDE PLAYBOOK (NEGOTIATE)
- 9.4 (orig 7.6): penalty only for wilful misconduct/gross negligence and inside cap. Playbook: outside cap, EUR 25,000/day minimum. High. Restore EUR 50,000 (fallback 25,000), outside cap, no fault test.
- 23.3 (orig SCC cl.15): "reasonable efforts to challenge" government requests; 23.2 "to the extent legally permissible." TIA relies on challenge commitment. High; restore cl.15 text, with best efforts to waive gag orders.
- 24.3, 24.5: immediate termination becomes 30 days; new early-termination fees under undefined "service order." High. Keep immediate termination for unauthorized transfers/sub-processing/regulator orders; no fees on data-protection terminations.
- 2.7 and Annex I catch-alls ("other processing," "other categories"): reject; Art 28(3), SCC Annex I.B need specificity.
- 2.2: "no legal analysis" and oral instructions. Accept oral instructions only if confirmed in writing; keep orig 5.1 duty to inform immediately. 
- 5.4, 20.3 cost reimbursement: accept for non-routine, pre-approved, reasonable costs; Art 28(3) does not itself mention remuneration. 11.3 regulatory-cooperation costs: reject for Eurocloud's own processing.
- 19.5 HIPAA warranty/"always lawful": limit to knowledge. Add HIPAA BAA check: PHI hosting by Eurocloud may need one (45 CFR 164.504(e)).
- 21.2: 15 business days' notice: reject for DPC (Art 31, 30(4)); Cascadia 5 days.
- 28.5 affiliate assignment: require notice, no change to locations/sub-processors, termination right.
- Annex I.C: keep SCC cl.13 supervisory authority fixed; Cascadia has no EU establishment, so confirm Art 27 representative and whether one-stop-shop applies.
- 3.2 and 17.4: 120-day non-renewal with only 90 days' price notice forces renewal before price known; require notice 30 days before non-renewal deadline. Fee escalation itself commercial (playbook 5.1).
- 4.6/18.1/18.2: accept mutual insurance, but restore Eurocloud EUR 20M/40M and 10-day evidence; stated EUR 25M must not cap liability.

PART 3 - WITHIN PLAYBOOK (ACCEPTABLE)
Recital I; 3.2 (120 days, tradeable); 8.2 "equivalent" (original Annex II already says "or stronger"); 8.3, 8.4, 22.1, 11.2 qualifier (tracks Art 28(3)(f)); 11.1 (5-day commitment binds Eurocloud); 14.2 for commercial information only (Personal Data confidentiality perpetual); 15.5 and 17.2 (orig 18.2, 22.3 already contain them; exclude breach-response costs from "indirect"); 16.4 (restore control-of-defense protections); 19.4 (add duty to notify legal change); 20.2; 25 force majeure (25.3 preserves data protection duties; exclude events DR/BCP should absorb); 27.2; witness lines; Annex II update right if notified.

PART 4 - NOT IN THE 47-CHANGE APPENDIX OR UNTRACKED
Tracked but omitted from appendix: 2.2 disclaimers (mislabeled 4.2), 11.1, 18.1-18.2, 19.5, 20.2-20.3, 21.2, 22.1, 23.2-23.3, 24.3-24.5, 25, 27.2, 28.5, 28.8, Annex I/II/III edits, TIA appendix. Untracked relative to April 14: remote-access ban (6.3), consent to any transfer (13.5), phased notice (7.3), regulator-contact 48h notice (11.1), subprocessor contract copy (8.3), remediation (15.6), Cascadia-held encryption keys (Annex II item 1; markup lists Eurocloud HSM key management, contradicting TIA split-key premise), Annex III addresses/transfer-mechanism column, 23.2(3) regulator-order termination, 28.7 SCC precedence. "Affiliate," "Services," "service order" undefined. TIA discrepancies: Northvault and Signalpath addresses differ (Annex III vs TIA 3.1); UK adequacy for Signalpath was due to lapse June 2025.

PART 5 - RISK MATRIX
Critical: breach (1); sub-processors (2); localization (3); transfers/TIA (4); audit (5); deletion (6); DPIA (9); SCC integrity (11); governing law (12); anonymization (13); baseline drift.
High: liability (7); indemnity (8); DPO (10); 9.4; 23.3; 24.3/24.5; catch-alls.
Medium: cost shifts; 21.2; 28.5; 19.5; 3.2/17.4; insurance; 2.2.
Low: Part 3.

PART 6 - STRATEGY (call May 28; signing June 6; outer limit late June)
Before call: your sign-off; Cascadia GC/CPO approval of fallbacks (TIA requires consultation); send compare demand.
Sequence: (1) Framework, standalone: governing law/forum, SCC integrity, localization/TIA (11, 12, 3, 4); without these nothing else is signable. Offer EU-state law choice and adequate-country DR. (2) Regulatory core: DPIA, audit, breach, deletion, anonymization. (3) Package trades: breach 36h/EUR 25,000 outside cap for restored audit; 3x super-cap for consequential-damages clause, mutual insurance, limited cost reimbursement; 60+30 deletion for certificate; general-authorization sub-processors for 30 days/partial termination. (4) Give freely: Part 3, 3.2, 17.4 (referred to commercial team), VAT, witnesses.
Leverage: runner-up bidder; Eurocloud's own Art 28(10)/83 exposure. Decision point about June 13: if framework items unresolved, invoke the two-week extension and warn of re-engagement.
Specialists: Irish counsel (fine-indemnity enforceability, courts, Irish DPC practice) now; Singapore/Brazil only if any non-EEA facility survives.
Also: SCC Module Two assumes a EU-to-non-EU exporter, but Eurocloud is the EU party and Cascadia the U.S. controller (subject to Art 3(2)); confirm module (Module Four/Art 3(2) issues) with Irish counsel before signing (unverified).
